profile.diet: Predatory fish; feeds on other fishes, squid and shrimp.
profile.behavior: Large, fast predator occurring from inshore coastal waters to offshore reef areas. Young barracuda are commonly found inshore in seagrass beds. Adults are top predators around reef habitat.
profile.habitat: Inshore to offshore; juveniles use seagrass beds, while larger fish range through coastal and reef environments.
profile.life_history: Native Florida species. The current FWC profile supports the habitat and feeding summary but does not establish a precise South Florida spawning calendar.

factors.value_notes: The previous numeric temperature bounds were not supported by a traceable species-specific thermal-preference source. They are retained unchanged for compatibility but should not be interpreted as a validated preferred range.

open_items: Species-specific preferred and limiting temperature ranges are not established by the cited FWC profile; current SST factor bounds remain provisional and unchanged.

regulations.summary: Collier through Martin counties, including Monroe, Miami-Dade and Broward: 15-36 in fork-length slot; one fish over 36 in allowed per person or vessel per day; 2 per person per day, maximum 6 per vessel; open year-round.
regulations.min_size: 15 inches fork length (Collier through Martin counties)
regulations.max_size: 36 inches fork length, with one fish greater than 36 inches allowed per person or vessel per day
regulations.bag_limit: 2 per person per day, maximum 6 per vessel per day; one fish over 36 inches may be retained per person or vessel per day
regulations.jurisdiction: Florida state and federal waters off Collier, Monroe, Miami-Dade, Broward, Palm Beach and Martin counties; other Florida counties have different/no barracuda-specific limits
regulations.source_name: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
regulations.notes: Special regulations apply inside Biscayne National Park. These South Florida county rules should not be generalized to the rest of Florida.
